title: myArticle
description:
A modern blog platform built with Nuxt 3 (Frontend) and Hono (Backend API).
Uses PostgreSQL as the main database and Redis for caching and view counters.
body: This blog is built as a system, not a stream. Each article is written with intent — to clarify thought, not to chase attention. The structure favors readability, the design removes distraction, and the performance remains consistent under use.

star.situation: I set out to build a full blog platform using Nuxt and Hono, aiming to handle real-world concerns such as caching, rate limiting, and structured APIs. However, my initial approach lacked a stable plan, causing friction during development.
star.task: Learn how to design and implement a complete system — from frontend to backend — with clear separation of concerns, reliable data flow, and maintainable structure.
star.action: I iterated through multiple architectural approaches, refining how the frontend communicates with the API, how data is modeled in PostgreSQL, and how Redis is used for caching and view tracking. I implemented RESTful patterns, enforced structure in routing and services, and gradually stabilized the system by removing unnecessary complexity and aligning components with their responsibilities.
star.result: The system evolved from inconsistency into a structured application with clear boundaries between layers. More importantly, I gained practical understanding of system design — not from theory, but from correcting flawed decisions. The result is not just a working platform, but a clearer approach to building the next one.

technicalFailures.title: Unstable Architecture
technicalFailures.what: I approached the system without a clear architectural direction, leading to frequent changes in structure, inconsistent patterns, and repeated rewrites across both frontend and backend.
technicalFailures.why: Planning was treated as optional. I moved directly into implementation without defining boundaries, responsibilities, or long-term structure.
technicalFailures.lesson: Architecture is not discovered mid-build. Decide the shape early, or rebuild it repeatedly later.

technicalFailures.title: Unfinished Testing
technicalFailures.what: I stopped testing once the system appeared to work. I forgot the principle that everything should be assumed broken until proven otherwise.
technicalFailures.why: I treated testing as optional. I did not prioritize it and viewed it as an afterthought.
technicalFailures.lesson: Testing is not a separate activity. Integrate it into development with clear goals and expectations.

technicalFailures.title: Complexity in Pipelines
technicalFailures.what: I did not separate complexity from the main codebase.
technicalFailures.why: I added new files to the codebase whenever tasks differed, instead of isolating them.
technicalFailures.lesson: In complex applications, separate CI and CD pipelines. Manage complexity outside the core codebase.

technicalFailures.title: Inconsistent Database Schema
technicalFailures.what: I used inconsistent database schema across environments.
technicalFailures.why: I did not standardize the schema across environments, leading to inconsistencies.
technicalFailures.lesson: Use a consistent database schema across environments to avoid inconsistencies.
